To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the M-RNA's extracted from mouse liver, kidney, spleen and thymus, and from rat liver, are heterogeneous with respect to size, and that the patterns of heterogeneity differ between tissues and species.
M-RNA is extracted in a form suitable for analysis from mouse liver, kidney and spleen, and that M-RNA's of different tissues show different patterns of synthesis in counter-current distribution.
M-RNA is present in mammalian tissues in the absence of protein, and that the M-RNA in mammalian tissues is a mixture of different species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, isolation, characterization, and fractionation of rapidly labelled M.R.N.A. from mammalian tissues.
the study of the synthesis, properties and metabolism of M-RNA's in mammalian tissues.
the isolation and characterization of M-RNA's and their distribution in mammalian tissues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the M-RNA preparations from rat liver, mouse liver, mouse spleen, mouse kidney, mouse thymus (pulsed in vitro) and mouse liver, spleens and kidney (pulsed simultaneously in vivo) have been characterized by the methods of sucrose density-gradient and counter-current distribution centrifugation.
the patterns obtained by counter-current distribution of M-RNA from rat and mouse tissues are reproducible and characteristic of the tissues and of the conditions of preparation.
M-RNA's are complex mixtures of molecules which differ from each other in their sedimentation coefficients and in their rates of synthesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
M-RNA is heterogeneous in its molecular weight, in its sedimentation coefficient and in the rate at which it is synthesized, and that these differences vary in different tissues.
M-RNA's extracted from different tissues and from different species show some common characteristics but also show some differences.
the counter-current distribution of rapidly labelled M- R-N-A from various mammalian tissues is reproducible under standard conditions and that the patterns are qualitatively similar.
The main takeaway from our work is that
M-RNA's extracted from various tissues by 4-amino salicylate-phenolic extraction procedures are complex mixtures.
the M-RNA from different tissues is qualitatively similar, but quantitatively different.
there is a great deal of heterogeneity in the patterns of M-RNA synthesis, both within and between tissues.
